newsitem.title: USA: United American unit ends management pact.
newsitem.headline: United American unit ends management pact.

text.p: United American Healthcare Corp said Friday that its U.A. Health Care of Ohio Inc (UAO) subsidiary agreed to terminate its management agreement with Personal Physician Care of Ohio Inc, a health maintenance organization (HMO) in Cleveland, Ohio.

In arbitration initiated by UAO, it was determined that its management agreement with Personal Physician would be discontinued effective June 1, 1997, seven months earlier than the company had expected as previously reported.

Historically, UAO's average annual fee revenue contribution to the company had been less than 10 percent. But enrollment rates and premium rates at Personal Physician were impacted by the state of Ohio's July 1996 Medicaid initiative, which mandated the enrollment of Medicaid recipients into managed care organizations and required premium reductions from the participating plans.
Over the last five fiscal years through May 31, 1997, UAO had contributed net earnings totaling $764,000.
"The termination of UAO's agreement with PPC allows us to reallocate resources to those subsidiaries in which we see future increased profitability," Julius Combs, chairman, said in a statement.
United American Healthcare is a full-service healthcare management company. It manages three HMOs under long-term contracts.
